app_profile_id.description: The unique name of the app profile in the form '[_a-zA-Z0-9][-_.a-zA-Z0-9]*'.
app_profile_id.rationale: `app_profile_id` is only a stable name for this profile in Terraform and APIs; it is not a credential or secret and does not determine who may call Bigtable—IAM does.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

description.description: Long form description of the use case for this app profile.
description.rationale: Free-text operator notes for consoles and audits; changing it does not alter routing rules, IAM bindings, or encryption settings.

ignore_warnings.description: If true, ignore safety checks when deleting/updating the app profile.
ignore_warnings.rationale: If true, bypasses safety warnings when deleting/updating the app profile. This is an IaC/operations lifecycle toggle whose risk is operational breakage, not an IAM, encryption, or data-exposure control; the two sibling `ignore_warnings` fields (gc_policy, schema_bundle) are correctly false and this should match.

instance.description: The name of the instance to create the app profile within.
instance.rationale: References which Bigtable instance this profile belongs to; instance names are identifiers in config/API and do not embed IAM grants.

multi_cluster_routing_use_any.description:
If true, read/write requests are routed to the nearest cluster in the instance, and will fail over to the nearest cluster that is available
in the event of transient errors or delays. Clusters in a region are considered equidistant. Choosing this option sacrifices read-your-writes
consistency to improve availability.
multi_cluster_routing_use_any.rationale: Controls routing/failover behavior for availability and consistency; it does not add principals to IAM or bypass authentication on the client API.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Non-secret project identifier used for API routing/billing context; it does not substitute for verifying callers or roles.

data_boost_isolation_read_only.description: Specifies that this app profile is intended for read-only usage via the Data Boost feature.

data_boost_isolation_read_only.compute_b.description: The Compute Billing Owner for this Data Boost App Profile. Possible values: ["HOST_PAYS"]
data_boost_isolation_read_only.compute_b.rationale: Billing attribution for Data Boost compute charges only; not an access-control attribute and does not contain secrets.

single_cluster_routing.allow_transaction.description:
If true, CheckAndMutateRow and ReadModifyWriteRow requests are allowed by this app profile.
It is unsafe to send these requests to the same table/row/column in multiple clusters.
single_cluster_routing.allow_transaction.rationale: Toggles whether CheckAndMutateRow/ReadModifyWriteRow transactional writes are permitted on a single-cluster-routing app profile. This is a data-consistency/correctness choice (avoiding unsafe cross-cluster transactional writes), not an access, encryption, exposure, or destructive-loss control, so a platform policy does not improve security.

single_cluster_routing.cluster_id.description: The cluster to which read/write requests should be routed.
single_cluster_routing.cluster_id.rationale: Names a cluster to receive traffic; it is a non-secret resource identifier. Who may read/write is still enforced by IAM and app credentials, not this string alone.

standard_isolation.description: The standard options used for isolating this app profile's traffic from other use cases.

standard_isolation.priority.description: The priority of requests sent using this app profile. Possible values: ["PRIORITY_LOW", "PRIORITY_MEDIUM", "PRIORITY_HIGH"]
standard_isolation.priority.rationale: QoS/priority tier only; it does not expose row data or widen who can authenticate to Bigtable.
